released.sort: from the first released to the most recent
released.era: Drop each console into the decade it came out.

rows.label: PlayStation 5
rows.description: Sony's ninth-generation and fifth home video game console
rows.hook: is Sony's current flagship home console, with a fast solid-state drive and a DualSense controller

rows.label: Nintendo Switch 2
rows.description: video game console developed by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the successor to a hugely popular hybrid handheld-and-home console, with larger magnetic-attach controllers

rows.label: Nintendo Switch
rows.description: hybrid video game console
rows.hook: is a hybrid console that docks to a TV or goes handheld, with detachable Joy-Con controllers

rows.label: PlayStation 2
rows.description: Sony's second home video game console, part of the sixth generation of consoles
rows.hook: is the best-selling home console of all time, and played DVDs out of the box

rows.label: PlayStation 4
rows.description: Sony's fourth home video game console, part of the eighth generation of consoles
rows.hook: is the Sony home console that outsold its Microsoft rival and added a Share button to its controller

rows.label: PlayStation 3
rows.description: video game console developed Sony Interactive Entertainment
rows.hook: is the Sony home console that launched with a Blu-ray drive and a very high price tag

rows.label: PlayStation
rows.description: 1994 5th generation video game console by Sony Interactive Entertainment
rows.hook: is the Sony console that moved games from cartridges to CDs and launched the company's gaming business

rows.label: Xbox Series X and Series S
rows.description: home video game consoles developed by Microsoft
rows.hook: is the pair of Microsoft consoles, one powerful and one budget-friendly digital-only model, launched together

rows.label: Nintendo Entertainment System
rows.description: third generation home video game console
rows.hook: is the 8-bit console that revived the American games industry after the crash, with a gray plastic zapper

rows.label: PlayStation Portable
rows.description: handheld game console by Sony
rows.hook: is Sony's handheld that played games on small optical discs and rivaled Nintendo's dual-screen device

rows.label: Xbox 360
rows.description: Microsoft's seventh-generation and second home video game console
rows.hook: is the Microsoft console known for online play over Live and the infamous red ring of death failure

rows.label: Wii
rows.description: seventh-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the console that got whole families swinging motion-sensing remotes to play bowling and tennis

rows.label: Nintendo DS
rows.description: Nintendo handheld game console
rows.hook: is the clamshell handheld with two screens, one of them a touchscreen used with a stylus

rows.label: Xbox One
rows.description: home video game console developed by Microsoft
rows.hook: is the Microsoft console that launched with a required motion camera and a heavy focus on TV features

rows.label: Nintendo 3DS
rows.description: portable 3D dual-screen handheld by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the handheld that showed 3D effects without glasses, and later got a bigger XL version

rows.label: Nintendo GameCube
rows.description: sixth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the purple cube-shaped home console that played small discs and had a carrying handle

rows.label: Nintendo 64
rows.description: fifth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the console with a three-pronged controller and four ports, home to Mario and Zelda in 3D

rows.label: Game Boy
rows.description: 1989 portable video game console
rows.hook: is the gray handheld with a green-tinted screen that made Tetris a worldwide phenomenon

rows.label: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the 16-bit console with a four-color-button controller, rival to Sega's blue-hedgehog machine

rows.label: Sega Genesis
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console developed by Sega
rows.hook: is the 16-bit console that raced a fast blue hedgehog against its Mario-hosting rival

rows.label: Dreamcast
rows.description: sixth-generation home video game console developed by Sega
rows.hook: is the last console from its maker, an early online-capable system with a controller holding a tiny screen

rows.label: Game Boy Advance
rows.description: handheld game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the landscape-shaped handheld successor to a green-screened original, with shoulder buttons

rows.label: PlayStation Vita
rows.description: portable game console developed by Sony Computer Entertainment
rows.hook: is Sony's second handheld, with a large OLED touchscreen and a rear touchpad

rows.label: Xbox
rows.description: video game console by Microsoft
rows.hook: is the first console from Microsoft, with a built-in hard drive and a famously huge controller

rows.label: Wii U
rows.description: eighth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: is the home console with a tablet-like touchscreen controller that struggled to find buyers

rows.label: Sega Saturn
rows.description: home video game console
rows.hook: lost the CD-era console race to a Sony rival and was notoriously hard to program

rows.label: Atari 2600
rows.description: home video game console by Atari
rows.hook: is the early cartridge console with a joystick and wood-grain panel that filled living rooms

rows.label: TurboGrafx-16
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console

rows.label: Nintendo DSi
rows.description: handheld game console by Nintendo

rows.label: Game Gear
rows.description: handheld game console developed by Sega
